subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-07T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap to confirm what we heard and the next steps so we all stay aligned. If I misunderstood anything, please flag.

Key pain points you shared:
- Frequent 95th pct latency spikes during peak windows (product search & chat flows) causing degraded UX.
- High concurrency bursts on market days (~200-300 RPS) with periodic short-lived spikes up to ~500 RPS.
- Model mix: currently using a tuned LLM for chat (fine-tuned Llama family) plus a smaller reranker for search; you want a path to a single-streamlined stack but fallback options are acceptable.

Goals / success criteria you mentioned:
- 95th percentile token latency for chat responses <= 300ms at typical 512-token sequences (goal; hard SLO to meet).
- Sustained throughput target: 200 RPS with burst headroom to 500 RPS for <5-minute windows.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer to avoid 2x increase in inference bill; looking for batching+cache recommendations.

Technical requirements we captured:
- Preferred model(s): Llama2-70B and Llama2-13B (for fallback/percentile planning).
- Support for quantized execution (int8/4) to reduce footprint where quality allows.
- VPC peering to your us-west cluster for Private deployment; if Hosted, region must be US-West (Oregon) for latency compliance.
- Audit logs and KMS integration required for any Private deployment.

Suggested deployment topology (initial proposal):
1) Dedicated Redwood pool in us-west with a mix of instances sized for 70B quantized serving + a smaller 13B pool for cost-efficient fallbacks.
2) Smart routing policy: route 90% traffic to 70B for full-quality responses; overflow / degraded mode routes to 13B.
3) Prefix/KV caching for common prompts and aggressive batching with per-customer queueing during peaks.
4) Canary rollout and automatic fallback to lower-capacity variants on CPU/GPU pressure.

Attachments: attached a draft SLO proposal and an architecture diagram for reference (redwood-slo-proposal.pdf, deployment-arch-diagram.png, sample-workload.json).

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
- Dev (cc'd) to run a short feasibility check on kernel and quantization compatibility with your fine-tuned model (action: Dev — by Thu 3/12).
- Alex to share sample 24-hour request traces and a representative set of prompts for quality checks (action: Alex — by Fri 3/13).
- I’ll follow up with a short pricing sketch and an updated SLO doc after Dev’s feasibility check (action: Marissa — by Mon 3/16).

If that looks right, I’ll prep the SOW-ish one-pager and a more detailed cost/throughput projection.

Thanks,

—Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>

Date: 2026-03-07T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns with our internal notes. A couple clarifications:

- The 300ms 95th is aspirational. If you can get 95th <= 400ms with clear degradation modes, that may be acceptable while we work on model optimizations.
- For bursts: 500 RPS is accurate but those are 1–3 minute spikes tied to promotional events.

I’ll upload the 24-hour traces and a sample prompt set to the Drive link you provided by Friday. For PCI/compliance reasons, we’ll scrub any customer-identifiable data (we already do).

Also, quick ask: can Dev call out any expected quality delta we should expect if we serve quantized 70B vs non-quantized? Even a ballpark is helpful for our PMs.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Sr. Engineering Manager, Product Platform
Acme AI

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-07T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Alex / Marissa — jumping in with the technical feasibility notes from our side after a quick look:

- Quantization impact: for Llama2-70B, int8 typically shows minimal semantic regression on chat-style prompts; int4 is more aggressive and can produce artefacts for highly detailed responses. We should run a quality eval set (your prompts) to measure perplexity / response similarity.
- Latency: achieving 95th <= 300–400ms at 512 tokens is possible with a combination of optimized kernels, continuous batching, and high-memory A100/HTX instances. Expect better tail latency if we keep sequence lengths lower or enable early-exit heuristics.
- Throughput: a dedicated GPU pool with batching can sustain ~200 RPS for 70B quantized on an appropriately sized fleet. For the 500 RPS short bursts, we'll rely on autoscaling + burst capacity; estimate cold-scale recovery time of ~90s unless we maintain some warm standby.
- Topology details: recommend 2 subpools: primary 70B-quantized (for quality) and secondary 13B-quantized (for cost & surge). Add prefix cache for top 10% of prompts.

Next technical items I need from Acme to produce a tighter estimate:
1) Representative prompt distribution (sample-workload.json helps).
2) Typical average sequence length and max tolerated truncation.
3) Any regulatory constraints on model weights (e.g., cannot export weights outside your tenancy) — affects Private vs Hosted.

I’ll spin up a quick benchmark plan and share expected latency/throughput curves by Monday. If we need, we can schedule a 30-min screen share to walk through kernel-level tradeoffs.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Dev. That plan sounds good — we’re okay with an initial 400ms 95th target if you can show the tradeoffs. I’ll get the sample traces uploaded today and confirm sequence length percentiles.

Let’s tentatively schedule the kernel/benchmark screen share for Tue 3/17 10am PT — Marissa / Naomi, does that work for you?

Thanks all,
Alex
